item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. Existing OneDrive, SharePoint, and security controls continue to govern access. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions.

For files uploaded through these experiences, Teams assigns permissions to chat participants for uploaded files. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control. 

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Users can already paste file links into external chats; this update makes attaching and sharing files easier within the policies your organization allows.
  • Admins can separately control the Teams attachment experience and automatic permission assignment using Teams PowerShell, as described below. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • Organizations that previously disabled in external chats
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach files (paperclip) option in external (federated) chats.
  • This change applies even if your organization previously configured this Teams setting as Disabled.
  • Organizations that want the Teams attachment experience in external chats to remain disabled must reapply the disabled setting after rollout.
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using Attach or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files uploaded through the attach or drag-and-drop experience.
  • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.
  • Disabling the Teams attachment experience does not prevent users from pasting file links; recipient access remains governed by the file’s permissions and applicable sharing policies.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

After rollout reaches your tenant, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams grants chat participants access to uploaded files before the message is sent, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

As part of our overall security initiatives, we’ve created a separate internal application configuration for Outlook attachments, therefore, all standard security and authentication flows will be handled separately. Moreover, Conditional Access policies are now enforced for Outlook attachment operations. Users who don’t meet company policies won’t be able to download, preview, or upload classic attachments (this includes inline images). Policies assigned to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be inherited by the attachment application by default. Continuous Access Evaluation is not included in the initial rollout but will follow up soon.

Scope: This change is only applicable to Outlook web (OWA) and New Outlook.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • Your existing policies now cover attachments. Conditional Access policies you have already scoped to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be enforced for attachment scenarios as well. No new policies need to be created.
  • Users out of compliance will be blocked from attachments. If a user's session no longer satisfies a Conditional Access policy — for example, a non-compliant device, a blocked location, or a network change that triggers CAE re-evaluation — attachment operations will be blocked.
  • These are separate follow-up changes we expect to land in the upcoming weeks. We’ll keep you updated on the readiness and rollout of these enhancements:
    • User sign in prompt for remediation. We're currently working on a solution to prompt the user for sign in to recover functionalities when possible. This will depend on the policy configuration; if the user is not compliant, they won’t be able to use attachment-related tasks. We’ll provide an update to customers once we start rolling out this enhancement.
    • Enable Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE). CAE isn’t supported for this new application configuration yet. We’ll update this message with additional content when it becomes available.  

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  1. Review how your Office and Exchange policies apply to attachments.
    1. Attachment operations are now handled by their own application, which by default inherits the Conditional Access policies you've assigned to Office and Exchange. Confirm those conditions are what you intend to enforce for attachments.
    2. If you’ve intentionally excluded Exchange online from a policy, that exclusion doesn't carry over to attachments, so users in scope can reach their mail but will be blocked from downloading, previewing, or uploading attachments.
    3. To manage attachment policies separate from mail, you can either exclude the attachment application from a policy or target it in a policy of its own. Both require a one-time setup step in your tenant — see Appendix: Excluding attachments from a policy.
  2. Update your help desk documentation. Support staff should know that attachment access failures may now result from a Conditional Access policy, and that the remediation is the same as for Outlook — return to a compliant device or network and re-authenticate.
  3. Notify users if you enforce strict Conditional Access policies, so they understand attachment actions may now be blocked under the same conditions that already block access to their mailbox.

[Appendix:]

Excluding attachments from a policy

Attachment operations are handled by an application named OwaDownloadAttachments (application Id: e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64 ). Before you can exclude it from a Conditional Access policy, a service principal for it must exist in your tenant. This is a one-time step you'll need to complete first.

Step 1: Create the service principal

You'll need the Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator role.

  1. Open Graph Explorer and sign in as an administrator of your tenant.
  2. Run:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals

Request body: { "appId": "e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64" }

Consent to Application.ReadWrite.All scope is required.

A successful request returns 201 Created with a display name of OwaDownloadAttachments. If the request reports that the service principal already exists, continue to Step 2.

Step 2: Exclude it from the policy

  1. Click on View or Edit on the Conditional Access Policy you want to update.
  2. Under Target resources, select the Exclude tab.
  3. Choose Select resources, search for OwaDownloadAttachments, and select it.
  4. Save the policy.

Repeat Step 2 for each policy you want attachment operations exempted from.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updatde the content. Thank you for your patience.

[What and why:]

We are evolving Microsoft Copilot to better connect the tools people rely on with the capablities they need to build, customize, and scale AI across work. Updates include a new Home experience and enhanced Office capabilities in the Copilot app; Code and Autopilot for building solutions and automating work; an enterprise-grade platform for running code; and updates to Copilot Notebooks, Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive, and Work IQ.

[Impact on your organization:]

Home in the Copilot app:

  • When users open the Copilot app, they will land in Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together on one screen. Users can switch between Chat and Cowork in the prompt box. Read more in the blog. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • As part of this update, we are making the following updates to the left navigation pane: 1) Plugins will replace the standalone Agents entry point (called Agents & Skills for some preview users) from Chat and the Customize entry point from Cowork. 2) For users with access to Cowork, Automations from Cowork will move to the Home navigation pane. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • Chat can complete long-running, multi-step knowledge work, including drafting email, managing meetings, working in Teams, managing OneDrive and SharePoint files, finding people, and creating Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and HTML files. Sensitive actions require user approval. Users can track and manage their long-running activity from Chat in the Tasks view, accessible in the upper right of the Copilot app navigation pane. These capabilities will roll out to Frontier later this month and are available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Chat will begin surfacing Skills that are used while generating responses, giving users greater transparency into how Copilot responds. This update will begin worldwide rollout in October and is available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Code:

  • The new Code experience gives users a dedicated place in the Copilot app to create trackers, dashboards, and apps using natural language. Users can access Code by going to the Code tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Code uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • Code is rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Autopilot:

  • Autopilot, previously called Scout, is an always-on personal agent in the Copilot app with persistent context, identity, and memory. Users can access Autopilot by going to the Autopilot tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Autopilot uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • We will update this message with rollout timing and admin control details when available.

Copilot app UI updates:

  • Cowork, Code, and Autopilot entry points in the Copilot app will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users that do not have a spending policy enabled will not be able to access these capabilities; instead, they will see an in-product message after clicking on the entry points to request access or learn more.
  • A new Microsoft 365 admin center setting will let admins choose whether users without a spending policy see Request Access or Learn More. Admins can configure whether or not users can request Copilot credits to use these experiences. Admins can also choose to block requests.
  • The existing setting in the admin center used to hide usage-based experiences (“Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing”) will be removed.
  • By default, enterprise users without a spending policy will see the “request access” message. Education users will see a Learn More link and cannot request access.
  • This update will roll out to standard customers in October and deferred customers in November.
  • To prepare: Review Microsoft 365 Admin center settings for usage-based experiences and spending policy. Decide if you want users without a spending policy to receive a "Request access" or "Learn more" message.

Full Office capabilities in the Copilot app:

  • Users can use full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint creation, editing, and collaboration capabilities in the Copilot app, side by side with Copilot. Users can also access recent Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from Library in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Capabilities accessed through Chat are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license. Capabilities accessed through Cowork use usage-based billing.
  • These capabilities are rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Copilot Managed Runtime:

  • Copilot Managed Runtime is an enterprise-grade platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary under IT governance. It supports apps built in Code, Cowork, Copilot Studio, and supported command-line and SDK experiences. Admins can manage these apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read more in the blog.
  • Managed Runtime is starting to roll out now into public preview.

Copilot Notebooks updates:

  • Copilot Notebooks will add task delegation, full Office editing and collaboration, interactive report creation, audio overview updates, model selection, and an updated user experience in the Copilot app and OneNote.
  • These updates will roll out to Frontier later this month.

SharePoint and OneDrive updates:

  • We are announcing the general availability of Copilot in SharePoint. The everyday AI capabilities that have been in public preview stay included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). New agentic capabilities and the ability to work at greater scale than was possible in preview will be available through usage-based billing (UBB) and consume Copilot Credits. We are also introducing general availability of Copilot in OneDrive, which follows the same licensing structure as SharePoint. Read more about Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive in the blog.
  • General availability begins rolling out later this month. Tenant availability may follow as rollout progresses.
  • To prepare: No action is required to continue using capabilities included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Admins can control who can access advanced SharePoint capabilities through UBB by going to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management. Existing cost management policies may automatically include newly available services. Existing PowerShell opt-out settings for the Public Preview of Copilot in SharePoint will continue to be honored until November 1st; after that, manage availability through SharePoint site AI settings.

Business Applications in Work IQ:

  • Work IQ now includes Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Power Platform data, enabling Copilot to ground responses and tasks on business and productivity data. Read more in the blog.
  • These updates will start rolling out in public preview later this month.
  • To prepare: Admins can configure Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data sources for Copilot in the Power Platform admin center. Admins can also manage the availability of business applications in Copilot in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings, and access through the Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) under Agents > Tools.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

In addition to the guidance listed in the individual updates above:

  • A spending policy is required for users to access capabilities available through Usage-based billing. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management. Educate users about usage-based billing scenarios and how to request access through IT. Learn more about spending policy and usage-based billing in the blog and message center post titled: Evolving Copilot pricing and new FinOps capabilities for AI.
  • Monitor this post for updated availability and deployment details.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by mid-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 15, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 (previously mid-August) and expect to complete by September 30, 2026 (previously mid-September).
  • GCC High: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 and expect to complete by September 30, 2026.
  • DoD: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 and expect to complete by October 30, 2026 (previously end of September).

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

Starting October 1, 2026, Exchange Web Services (EWS) will be gradually disabled in line with previous communications linked to this message. As this rollout reaches your tenant, cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing that rely on EWS will be affected — recipients in partner organizations may no longer see Free/Busy, MailTips, or shared calendars from your tenant. 

If your organization is not ready to migrate, you can retain EWS access by following the guidance of the latest blog we published: ExchangeOnline EWS, Your Time is Almost Up (EWSEnabled set to True) while you prepare and execute the migration steps attached to this message. EWS access through this extension will remain available until the final EWS shutdown on April 1, 2027. 

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Follow this Message center post for updates to the rollout schedule. To avoid impact, plan to migrate after the rollout reaches your tenant and before EWS deprecation.
  • Review the migration guide linked below for step-by-step instructions to understand your current configurations, set up new Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policies, validate the new configurations, and remove unused configurations. 
  • Check the blog post linked below for additional information and answers to frequently asked questions. 
  • Hybrid and on-premises scenarios are not in scope. This update applies to fully cloud-hosted (Exchange Online ↔ Exchange Online) cross-tenant and cross-cloud configurations only. For organizations running on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online in a Hybrid Deployment, migrate to Dedicated Hybrid App. For organizations hosted in Exchange Online sharing with another organization running Exchange on-premises, kindly monitor future Message Center posts for guidance on migration paths as they become available. 

[Additional information:]

  • Migration guide: Migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy for sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips.
  • Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy Microsoft Graph API Overview
  • Exchange Online EWS, Your Time is Almost Up
  • Deprecation of EWS in Exchange Online 
  • Enhancing Microsoft 365 security by eliminating high-privilege access 
  • Blog Post: Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing are moving to Cross-Tenant Access Policy

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Users can temporarily pause all notifications
item.description:

Platforms:

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Microsoft 365 admin center: Agent Registry consolidates duplicate agent entries and adds version history
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We're improving the Agent Registry experience in the Microsoft 365 admin center by consolidating duplicate entries for the same agent into a single record. Previously, the same agent could appear multiple times when published across different scopes or when multiple published versions existed.

This update simplifies agent governance, provides a clearer inventory of deployed agents, and makes it easier for admins to manage agent lifecycle and version history from a single location. All versions of an agent will be accessible from the agent details flyout while governance actions continue to apply across the entire agent.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide: Beginning in mid-September 2026 and expected to complete in mid-October 2026 (previously late September)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Global Administrators
  • Global Readers
  • AI Administrators
  • Organizations using the Agent Registry

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Agent Registry

What will happen

  • Each agent will appear only once in the Agent Registry.
  • Agents that previously appeared as multiple entries due to different publishing scopes or published versions will be consolidated into a single entry.
  • The Registry list will display the most recently published organizational version by default.
  • Selecting an agent will open an agent details flyout that includes a version selector.
  • The version selector will display available published versions and any in-progress draft versions where applicable. Selecting a version will update the agent details shown in the flyout.
  • Governance actions, such as Block, will continue to apply to the entire agent across all versions.
  • Total agent counts in the Agent Registry may decrease because duplicate entries are being consolidated. No agents are being removed.
  • Reports, dashboards, exports, and custom processes that relied on previous per-entry counts may show different totals after rollout.
  • Registry exports will include options for exporting agents and their associated versions.
  • This change is enabled by default and requires no configuration.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that administrators:

  • Inform governance and operations teams that Agent Registry counts may decrease as duplicate entries are consolidated.
  • Review internal reports, dashboards, scripts, and processes that depend on Agent Registry counts or export data.
  • Update internal documentation and training materials to reflect the new version selector experience in the agent details flyout.
  • Validate any downstream reporting that uses Agent Registry export data after rollout is complete.

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Agent Registry counts will change because duplicate entries are consolidated. Reports, dashboards, exports, and other administrative reporting based on prior count logic may show different totals after rollout.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Personal message reminders for chat and channels

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Updates to Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) Quotas for New, Trial, and Education Tenants
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

To strengthen protection against abuse and ensure fair use of Exchange Online resources, we are updating how the Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) quota is calculated for certain tenants.

These changes improve how quotas account for tenant age (how long the tenant has existed since creation), trial subscriptions, and educational organizations using free Education (EDU) licenses.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rolling out beginning mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by end of November 2026. 

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Newly created tenants (first 60 days)
  • Trial tenants
  • Educational organizations with free EDU licenses

Platforms/Services:

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange admin center (EAC)

What will happen:

TERRL quota calculations will change based on tenant status and licensing.

  • New tenant quotas (based on tenant age):
    • Less than 31 days: 10% of standard calculated quota
    • 31–60 days: 25% of standard calculated quota
    • More than 60 days: 100% of standard calculated quota
  • Trial tenants:
    • Daily TERRL quota reduced from 5,000 to 500 external recipients
  • Tenants with free EDU licenses (e.g. A1 licenses):
    • New formula applied: 500 × (Purchased Email Licenses^0.7 + Free EDU Licenses^0.3) + 9500
    • Free EDU licenses contribute to the quota at a lower weighting than purchased licenses
  • Tenants without free EDU licenses:
    • Existing formula remains unchanged: 500 × (Purchased Email Licenses^0.7) + 9500

If a tenant exceeds its quota:

  • Additional outbound messages to external recipients will be blocked until usage falls below the rolling 24-hour limit
  • Senders will receive one of the following Non-Delivery Reports (NDRs):
    • Trial tenants: 550 5.7.232 — Message blocked due to trial tenant external recipient limit
    • Non-trial tenants: 550 5.7.233 — Message blocked due to tenant external recipient limit

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the Tenant Outbound External Recipients Rate report in the Exchange admin center: EAC > Reports > Mail flow > Tenant Outbound External Recipients Rate.
  • Monitor:
    • Current TERRL quota
    • Outbound recipient volume
    • Percentage of quota consumed
    • Blocked recipients (if any)
    • TERRL enforcement status
  • If your organization regularly operates near or above quota consider migrating high-volume, application-driven outbound email to a third-party bulk email service or purchasing more licenses to cover your volume needs.

Learn more: Introducing Exchange Online Tenant Outbound Email Limits

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra ID: Enhance protection of the authentication experience by blocking external script injection
item.description:
[What and why]

As part of Microsoft's Secure Future Initiative, we are strengthening the security of the Microsoft Entra ID sign-in experience by introducing additional Content Security Policy (CSP) protections. This change helps protect users from threats such as cross-site scripting (XSS) by allowing only trusted Microsoft-hosted scripts to run during authentication and blocking unauthorized or externally injected code.

This post is a reminder of our previous announcement (MC1191924), which communicated this upcoming security change and the actions organizations may need to take before rollout. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in mid-October 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations whose users authenticate through Microsoft Entra ID sign-in pages hosted on login.microsoftonline.com
  • Organizations using browser extensions, monitoring tools, customization tools, or other solutions that inject scripts into the sign-in experience
  • Microsoft Entra External ID tenants are not affected

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Web-based authentication experiences using login.microsoftonline.com
  • Browser-based sign-in experiences across supported browsers

What will happen

  • A new Content Security Policy (CSP) header will be added to Microsoft Entra ID sign-in pages.
  • Scripts will be permitted only from trusted Microsoft content delivery network (CDN) domains.
  • Inline script execution will be restricted to trusted Microsoft-authorized sources.
  • Browser extensions and tools that inject scripts into Microsoft Entra ID sign-in pages may stop functioning.
  • Users will continue to be able to sign in even if unsupported script injection tools no longer function.
  • This change is enabled by default as part of the service update and does not require tenant configuration.
  • Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) and API-based authentication flows are not affected because CSP enforcement applies only to browser-based sign-in experiences using login.microsoftonline.com.

[Action required and recommendations]

If your organization does not use tools or extensions that inject code into Microsoft Entra ID sign-in pages, no action is required.

If your organization uses tools that inject code into the sign-in experience:

  • Review the CSP guidance and assess whether any tools, browser extensions, or custom solutions rely on script injection.
  • Test affected authentication workflows ahead of rollout.
  • Replace or update any solutions that depend on script injection into Microsoft Entra sign-in pages.
  • Communicate potential impacts to help desk and identity administration teams.
  • Update internal documentation if it references affected authentication customizations.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated September 25, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

We will begin rolling out this feature late September 2025. Rollout timeline for phase 3 will be announced later.

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

For tenants with agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, a wizard in the Teams admin center will help identify affected agents and apps and guide through resolving discrepancies.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unify app installation across admin centers

In this phase, app and agent installation management is unified across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Admins can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, and changes remain synchronized across both admin centers.

No additional action is required by admins. Existing installation assignments will be synchronized across both admin centers for eligible tenants.

Eligible tenants: Any tenant that moved to the unified availability state as part of Phase 1 or Phase 2, or moves as part of Phase 3 in the future, will automatically receive this feature once unified.

Timeline: We will release this feature end of September 2026 for eligible tenants.

Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. App installations previously made through app setup policies are not unified as part of this change.

  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567883

How this will affect your organization

Before this rollout, managing Teams apps that also work in Outlook and the Microsoft 365 app was fragmented across two admin centers:

  • the Integrated apps and Agent apps pages in the Microsoft 365 admin center, and
  • the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

This sometimes resulted in inconsistent availability settings for the same app.

With Unified agent app management, admins can manage apps and agents from either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. Availability settings will remain synchronized across both, ensuring a consistent management experience.

What you can expect:

  • You’ll gain a consolidated view of agent and Microsoft 365 app availability across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.
  • Changes made in either admin center to the agent and app availability will automatically apply across all supported hosts.
  • Organization-wide defaults for both admin centers will be in sync and govern app availability across Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 copilot app.

What you need to do to prepare

To ensure a smooth transition, review your tenant-level and individual agent/app settings (app allow/block & user availability) in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center and the Teams Admin Center. If different departments within your organization manage these settings, we suggest coordinating efforts to complete the review collaboratively.

This update will be rolled out automatically by the stated date, and no immediate action is required. However, it's a good time to update any internal documentation related to agent and app management policies.

Learn more: Unified agent and app availability management across Microsoft 365 and Teams Admin Centers - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: Evolving the Copilot pricing model and new FinOps capabilities for AI
item.description:
[What and why:]

We are evolving Copilot pricing model as AI gets more capable with longer and more complex work. Everyday AI remains covered by the Copilot user subscription license (USL), priced per user per month, including model selection and Auto, which weighs accuracy, speed, and cost on each request to route to the model and level of reasoning effort best suited to the job. Advanced AI, including new advanced frontier models, may now be available through usage-based billing (UBB) with Copilot Credits. For more information, read Evolution of the Copilot pricing model.

Users may encounter UBB:

  • When using a frontier model or advanced AI or
  • When they hit a limit, with an option to extend their use through Copilot Credits

UBB capabilities will be visible to all end users, however these capabilities are not enabled or functional within Enterprise tenants until an admin creates a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Only then will credits to use UBB features by consumed.

You can control and manage consumption billing across your organization through the admin policies, spending limits, and monitoring tools you configure.

We are also releasing new FinOps for AI capabilities to help you understand and manage usage, connect cost to value, and make informed decisions: 

  • Cost management in Microsoft 365 admin center is expanding beyond Copilot Cowork and Work IQ APIs to support Copilot Code, Copilot Managed Runtime, and advanced work for SharePoint and OneDrive in Copilot. In October, support will also extend to agents built through Microsoft Copilot Studio.
  • When configuring a spending policy in Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can assign models and effort levels by group to balance cost and business impact, including which models Auto can select in Cowork. This capability is rolling out for Cowork, with more workloads planned.
  • The consumption dashboard in Insights is designed to help leaders get a clearer view of how Cowork helps their teams complete meaningful work—not just how often they use it. By connecting credit consumption with outcomes, organizations can identify high-value scenarios and compare results with the resources invested.
  • End users can view their UBB spend within the Cowork experience with the ability to see credit usage, remaining credits, and credit history, with banners alerting them as they approach their limits.
  • Administrators can now edit billing methods for existing spend policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

For more additional information, read New FinOps for AI capabilities: Control spend, measure value, and optimize for impact.

Learn more about new features coming to Copilot, including advanced capabilities in SharePoint which will roll out with UBB, in the Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365 message center post.

[Rollout schedule:]

UBB will begin to roll out in Copilot in Q4 CY2026. UBB will also be enabled as part of the Frontier public preview experience.

All FinOps capabilities listed above are available in preview in September 2026. End-user visibility into Copilot Credit usage, remaining credits, and credit history is generally available in September 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Administrators can use cost management in the Microsoft 365 admin center to manage usage-based billing, assign access and spending policies, monitor Copilot Credit usage and spend, view remaining credit capacity, and set limits and alerts. Controls may vary by service.

Users will see frontier models and advanced AI with UBB in Copilot as those features become available. UBB capabilities are visible in product by default. If a user has a spending policy assigned to them, they will be able to consume Copilot Credits as part of UBB.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • No action is required to continue using capabilities included as part of the USL
  • Manage usage-based billing and Copilot Credit consumption by configuring spending policies.

Additional Information

  • Understanding the user subscription license (USL) and usage-based billing (UBB)
  • Usage-Based Billing and Cost Management for Copilot Credits
  • Managing AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing
  • Discovery setting for AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing
  • Copilot Credits Licensing Guide

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed? New frontier models and advanced AI capabilities may process existing Microsoft 365 content when used through Copilot experiences. 
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with customer data? These changes include new frontier models and advanced AI capabilities through usage-based billing and introduce model selection controls, Auto model selection governance, and expanded AI workload support. 
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Users can access frontier models, advanced AI experiences, and usage-based extensions when limits are reached. The embedded spend management experience also exposes consumption information directly within the Copilot experience. 
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities? New FinOps capabilities expand cost management, consumption monitoring, spending policies, model assignment by group, outcome measurement, and credit consumption reporting. Administrators gain additional oversight and governance controls.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] SharePoint: Improved site metadata size reporting
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is improving how site metadata size is reported in SharePoint. The calculation will include document library field data, giving admins a more complete view of a site’s metadata usage.

Nothing about your content changes. No content is added, moved, or removed, and the site metadata size limit remains 1 TB per site.

Because the calculation is more complete, reported metadata size may be higher for some sites. For most sites, the difference will be small and nothing else will change. Some sites may show a size at or above the 1 TB limit once the updated calculation is applied.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability, Worldwide: We will begin rolling out on October 20, 2026.
  • Sites already identified as expected to reach or exceed the 1 TB metadata limit will be excluded from the initial rollout to provide additional time to reduce their metadata usage before the correction is applied.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • SharePoint admins who monitor site storage and metadata usage.
  • Organizations with SharePoint sites that are close to or above the 1 TB site metadata limit.
  • Site owners and users of sites that receive metadata warnings or enforcement messages.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint Online.
  • SharePoint Storage Metrics.
  • SharePoint document libraries and lists.

What will happen:

  • Most organizations will see no change in behavior.
  • The visible difference is that reported site metadata size may be higher than before because document library field data is included in the calculation.
  • For sites that cross the 1 TB metadata limit after the correction, the site is blocked from adding new metadata until usage is brought back under the limit.
  • Existing content stays in place and remains accessible.
  • SharePoint shows a warning or error message when the site is close to, or has reached, the metadata limit.
  • For sites that reach 80% of the metadata limit, admins can review the metadata size breakdown on the Storage Metrics page.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is needed for most organizations.

If you see a metadata warning for a site, review its metadata usage and take steps to reduce it:

  • Check the Storage Metrics page for the site. For sites at or above 80% of the metadata limit, the metadata size breakdown is available on this page.
  • Delete unneeded items from your lists and document libraries.
  • Delete older file versions in your document libraries.
  • Remove duplicate files across lists and libraries.
  • Follow the steps provided in the in-product warning message.
  • Re-check the Storage Metrics page after making changes.

If a site remains over the 1 TB metadata limit after the correction is applied, the site will be blocked from adding new metadata until usage is reduced below the limit. Existing content will remain accessible.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. SharePoint metadata size reporting will include document library field data, giving admins a more complete view of site metadata usage. Content is not added, moved, or removed.
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. Sites that exceed the 1 TB metadata limit can be blocked from adding new metadata until usage is reduced below the limit, which may affect creation or update actions that add metadata.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Admins will see a more complete metadata size calculation on the Storage Metrics page and may see warning or error messages when a site is close to or over the limit.

item.title: [planForChange] Final reminder: Microsoft Project Online retires on September 30, 2026
item.description:
[What and why:]

Microsoft Project Online will retire on September 30, 2026.  

If users are still using Project Online, they will see an in-app banner announcing the retirement. 

If your organization will not be fully migrated by September 30, 2026, we highly recommend you contact a Microsoft partner immediately to make a migration plan and let your Microsoft account team know your plans.  

At Microsoft, we are committed to empowering every organization with a unified, AI-powered and collaborative work management experience that brings together tasks, plans, and projects in one seamless platform. As part of this commitment, we announced the retirement of Project Online last September. The decision reflects our focus on delivering solutions that are modern, scalable, and future-ready—enabling organizations to benefit from the latest innovations in AI, automation, and collaboration.  Moving to our next-generation platforms brings enhanced productivity, deeper integration with Microsoft 365, and new capabilities designed for the way people work today and tomorrow. 

This update is exclusive to Project Online and does not affect Project desktop/Project Online desktop, Project Server, or Planner.  

We recognize that every organization is unique, with different project management needs and technical requirements. To ensure a smooth transition and continued success, Microsoft is providing three clear paths forward. 

  1. Microsoft Planner: For organizations seeking a modern, cloud-first, and AI-powered project management experience, Planner is designed for flexibility, collaboration, and scalability—empowering teams to manage everything from simple tasks to complex projects in one unified platform. The premium features of Planner included in our Planner and Project Plan 3 license, offer advanced features such as portfolios, baselines, dependencies, and Gantt charts. 
  2. Project Server Subscription Edition: For organizations with advanced project and portfolio management (PPM) requirements, or those needing a short-term solution before moving to the cloud, Project Server Subscription Edition offers comprehensive tools for planning, scheduling, and resource management—built on the latest SharePoint Server technology. 
  3. Project Operations: For Dynamics ERP customers, especially those focused on timesheets and resource scheduling. 

[Rollout schedule:]

Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD:  September 30, 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • After Project Online is retired, you will no longer be able to access your projects or any associated data within the service.  
  • To avoid disruption and potential data loss, it's essential that you complete your transition to any of the alternatives before the retirement date. 
  • You can get details about your organization's Project Online usage by following the Export user data from Project Online documentation.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  • Identify a Microsoft Partner immediately to help you move off Project Online by month end. To find a partner, contact your Microsoft Sales Representative for a list of recommended partners in your region. 
  • Evaluate the alternatives proposed above and plan the transition immediately. 
  • Migrate your data, if needed, before the retirement date. 
  • This retirement will happen automatically on the specified dates with no admin action required. 
  • You may want to notify your users and update any internal documentation to reflect the above changes. 
  • Review documentation to learn more about how to Prepare for Project Online retirement.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams Rooms: Identify in-room participants with IntelliFrame people labels
item.description:
Updated September 24, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

We're introducing IntelliFrame people labels in Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows to improve meeting clarity and inclusivity for remote participants. When enabled, this feature identifies in-room participants by name and displays a contact card, helping remote attendees easily recognize speakers and follow conversations.

This enhancement supports better hybrid meeting experiences by connecting in-room and remote participants more effectively, improving collaboration and productivity.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566700.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October) expected to complete by mid-December 2026 (previously late October)

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams Rooms on Windows with Teams Rooms Pro licenses
  • In-room participants who have enrolled in voice and face recognition (People Recognition)

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams Rooms on Windows devices
  • Supported intelligent camera hardware

What will happen:

  • IntelliFrame will display name labels under identified in-room participants’ video feeds.
  • Remote participants can select a label to view a contact card with organizational details.
  • The feature is enabled automatically when prerequisites are met.
  • Existing Teams meeting policies for voice and face enrollment are honored.
  • Participants without enrolled profiles will appear without labels.
  • No change occurs if voice and face enrollment is disabled in your organization.

Screenshot - IntelliFrame people labels identify enrolled in-room participants by name, helping remote attendees recognize who's speaking; selecting a label opens the person's contact card

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required to enable this feature.

To maximize value, administrators may:

  • Review and confirm Teams Rooms devices:
    • Ensure devices are licensed with Teams Rooms Pro.
    • Verify use of supported intelligent cameras.
  • Review and update meeting policies:
    • Allow enrollment: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Enabled.
    • Enable name display in rooms: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride On.
  • Encourage users to enroll in voice and face recognition: Teams > Settings > Recognition.
  • Update internal documentation and helpdesk guidance.
  • Notify users about this capability to drive awareness and adoption.

To disable IntelliFrame people labels, administrators can:

  • Turn off in-room name display (labels stop; other IntelliFrame framing unaffected): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -RoomPeopleNameUserOverride Off
  • Block voice and face enrollment entirely (no one can be identified by name): Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -EnrollUserOverride Disabled
  • Individual users can opt out anytime by removing their profile in Teams > Settings > Recognition.

Learn more: 

  • What is Microsoft Multi-Stream IntelliFrame and Intelligent Camera? | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Enable People Recognition on Teams Rooms (voice & face policies) | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)
  • Overview and configuration of voice and face enrollment | Microsoft Learn (will be updated before rollout)

[Compliance considerations:]

Compliance AreaImpact
Introduces or modifies AI/ML capabilitiesUses AI-based biometric identification (voice and face profiles) to identify in-room participants. Identification occurs only for users who have consented and completed People Recognition enrollment.
Stores new customer dataThis feature does not create new data; it relies on existing voice and face profiles from People Recognition enrollment, governed by the organization’s current configuration.
Alters processing of existing customer dataParticipant identity data is processed differently when recognition is enabled.
Provides new way of communicating between usersLabels and contact cards enhance visibility of in-room participants for remote users.
Adds or changes admin controlsControlled via Teams meeting policies (EnrollUserOverride and RoomPeopleNameUserOverride).
